business_summary.text: Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited is a Miniratna Defence public sector undertaking that makes titanium alloys, superalloys and high-strength steels for aerospace, defence, space and energy applications.

call_points.text: FY27 growth to exceed FY26's, but Q1's 40% run-rate is not practicable for the full year.
FY27 capex guided at only ₹50-60 Cr, mostly maintenance.
S400 certification from GE USA received on 13 August; revenue potential to be known a couple of quarters later.
Aluminium plant JV with NALCO recommended for closure by both boards; awaiting ministry approval.
Metal bank is customer-owned and MIDHANI-operated, so it does not sit on MIDHANI's books or release working capital.
Margins depend on product mix; super alloy and titanium carry higher margins than special steel.
FY27 revenue growth targeted at 15%, with bottom line up about 20%.
Open order book ₹2,250 Cr; ₹1,500 Cr of orders expected in FY27.
About ₹1,000 Cr capex planned over three years, mostly downstream forging and rolling equipment.
Metal bank for six critical raw materials expected within four months.
Spring plant to be fully operational in a month or two; no orders yet.
Titanium and maraging steel carry higher margins than superalloys; mix drives margins.
Capex to be funded through operating leases and term loans; no major funding issues foreseen.
Raw material and energy supply disruptions could delay orders.
Management declined to give alloy-wise gross margins, calling the data confidential.
Exports were ₹85 Cr in FY26; at least ₹100 Cr expected in FY27.
AMCA alloy development work has started; production orders expected after development.

About ₹1,500 Cr of orders expected to be booked in FY27.

operating_notes.text: Titanium production reached about 700 tonnes in FY26, almost double the previous year.
Titanium orders exceed ₹660 Cr; defence is 79% of the order book.
The ₹40 Cr fastener plant expects ₹20-30 Cr of orders a year from the missile and space sectors.
Order book of ₹2,329 Cr as on 1 July 2026, with defence at 66%, space/ISRO 21%, energy 9% and others 4%.
Titanium orders worth about ₹600 Cr in hand; 750 tonnes melted last year at the new titanium facility.
Scrap inventory reduced by ₹17 Cr in Q1FY27, after a ₹75 Cr reduction last year.

timeline.summary: On June 3, 2026, MIDHANI's Q4FY26 call guided FY27 revenue growth of 15% and EBITDA margin of 23-25%, with a ₹2,250 Cr order book and about ₹1,000 Cr of capex planned over three years.
On 17 August 2026, MIDHANI's Q1FY27 call reported revenue up 40.46% to ₹239.49 Cr and PAT up 27.42% to ₹16.31 Cr, with EBITDA margin at 20% on LPG and raw-material cost inflation.
